doc.title: Albert Warner and Sonny Henry Interview, 1959-01-08

title: Lessons with Arthur Steve, practising while pressing, and the Bulls Band
summary: He took lessons from Arthur Steve, practised between pressing jobs, and joined Giles's neighbourhood brass band, helped by Pete.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: No, never worried about music. I had the opportunity to learn to play piano, but I was a fast man at the time. Didn't have time to worry with music. See, and, uh, so after that, uh, I went and bought the method and started going up there twice a week. So finally, I got the first, second, and third position and learned how to make those notes in the end. So, uh, after he left, I went with Steve. Well, Steve, well, he wasn't a great musician. Well, I went on to him and taken a couple of lessons with him. So he played a trombone tune. Steve. Yeah. Steve. What was his last name? What was Steve's last name, Sonny? Arthur. Arthur Steve. Yeah. Yeah. That's his first name, Arthur. Yeah. Yeah. Arthur Steve. He lived right around here in Phillips street. He's still living. No, he's dead now. Yeah. And, uh, so I taken a couple of lessons with him. So finally, uh, Giles was putting up a band, Clay Giles' brother. Well, uh, after I learned, but before that, I got a self-instructor. A fella sent off to New York and got me a self-instructor. Well, I went on and I started a practice, not the self-instructor. So at the time I was in the pressing business too, and still working where I'm at, where I just retired from. And, uh, yeah. And so every time I'd blow the horn, I'd lay it down, I'd go press a piece. I'd come back, blow the horn, go back and press another piece. And my wife says, gee whiz, you say, you make me sick with this thing. I said, well, I might make you sick now. I said, but someday this thing will come in handy because I'd find out what it was all about. You see? So, uh, finally, after I kind of got good with it, Giles came along. He wanted me to join a little band that was putting up a little brass band back on that street. So I went on it with the brass, brass band and so they call it the Bulls Band. So I used to rehearsal with them every Sunday. So this same boy, what he was talking about, Pete, what we call him, being the pit, be a pee picker, huh? Yeah. And I used to go by Pete and Pete used to help me out a whole lot, you know, and he'd show me a different thing because he used to come around the band too. Well, what part of town were you born? Did you give that street? Well, uh, right around, uh, Sinan and Roman.

Part most of your life. I brought up around this neighborhood, right around what they call the Tremie, you see? Mm-hmm. I brought up around this, uh, neighborhood, yeah. And, uh, so bring back this, uh,
